sections.label: A
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.citation: CY 2021 AAR, Executive Summary, Section A, p. i
sections.text:
The City of Manila was founded on June 24, 1571, as a municipal government. It became the first chartered City by virtue of the Philippine Commission Act 183 on July 31, 1901, and gained autonomy with the passage of Republic Act (RA) No. 409 or the “Revised Charter of the City of Manila” on June 18, 1949.

sections.label: D
sections.heading: Scope and Objectives of Audit
sections.citation: CY 2021 AAR, Executive Summary, Section D, p. iv
sections.text: The audit covered the accounts and operations of the City of Manila for the period January 1 to December 31, 2021. The objectives of the audit are to: (a) be able to lend credence to Management’s assertions on the financial statements; (b) recommend agency improvement opportunities; (c) determine compliance with existing laws, rules and regulations; and (d) determine the extent of implementation of prior years’ audit recommendations.

sections.label: E
sections.heading: Independent Auditor’s Report on the Financial Statements
sections.citation: CY 2021 AAR, Executive Summary, Section E, pp. iv-v
sections.text:
The Auditor rendered a qualified opinion on the fairness of presentation of the financial statements due to the deficiencies noted in the audit that materially affected the balances/totals of certain accounts, which are discussed in detail in Part II of the report and summarized as follows:
1. Accounting errors overstated the Cash-in-Bank (CiB) accounts by P51.371 million mainly because of the: (a) absence of an effective reconciliation of the records of the Office of the City Accountant (OCAT) and City Treasurer’s Office (CTO); (b) inability of the accounting application to capture the standard transaction descriptions and references and produce the prescribed primary and subsidiary records that provide the audit trails; and (c) breakdowns in the bank reconciliation. Thus, overstated the carrying amounts of the CiB accounts by a net amount of P51.371 million.
We reiterated our recommendation that Management:
a. Direct the OCAT to correct the accounting errors which resulted in overstatement of the carrying amounts of the CiB accounts by a net amount of P51.371 million;
b. Direct the OCAT and CTO to reconcile fully their CiB records with those of the depository banks; and
c. Address the deficiencies of the Philippine Public Sector Accounting Standards (PPSAS) System used by OCAT to ensure that it captures, processes and reports all disbursement transactions of the City with the standard audit trails.
We also recommended that Management fast track the implementation of the new accounting application system for efficient, valid, accurate and complete processing of financial transactions.
2. The City had not settled cash advances totaling P182.725 million contrary to Section 89 of Presidential Decree No. 1445 and COA Circular No. 97-002 dated February 10, 1997, and bear on the fair presentation of the affected accounts in the Financial Statements (FS).
We recommended that Management:
a. Enforce the liquidation of the cash advances and, henceforth, enforce strictly the liquidation of cash advances within the prescribed period; and
b. Record in the book of accounts the liquidations of cash advances amounting P641,630.33 and, prospectively, promptly record the liquidations of cash advances in order to reflect them in the books of accounts in the proper period.
3. Payables amounting to P21.888 million were not supported with the required documents proving their validity, thus, casting doubt on the fairness of the presentation of the payable accounts in the City’s FS.
In order to present fairly the Accounts Payable account in the FS, we recommended that Management direct the OCAT, in coordination with the City General Services Office, to:
a. Submit all the lacking documentation of the payables amounting to P21,887,936.93;
b. Establish if the payables amounting to P1,625,539,630.64 are indeed firm liabilities to pay, otherwise, revert them to the surplus; and
c. Specify in the schedule of payables the correct addresses of all the concerned creditors.
The aforementioned observations together with the corresponding recommendations were discussed with Management officials concerned during the exit conference on June 8, 2022. Management views and comments were incorporated in the report, where appropriate.

sections.label: F
sections.heading: Summary of Suspensions, Disallowances and Charges as of year-end
sections.citation: CY 2021 AAR, Executive Summary, Section F, p. vi
sections.text: The audit suspensions, disallowances and charges amounting to P42.538 million, P67.2 million and P33.047 million, respectively, remained unsettled by the concerned officers/employees and third parties determined to be liable thereto due to the inability of the Management to fully enforce settlement of the same as required under Section 7.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009.

sections.label: G
sections.heading: Status of Implementation of Prior Years’ Audit Recommendations
sections.citation: CY 2021 AAR, Executive Summary, Section G, p. vi
sections.text: Of the 58 prior years’ audit recommendations contained in the CYs 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2020 Annual Audit Reports, 17 or 29.31 percent were fully implemented, 25 or 43.10 percent were partially implemented and 16 or 27.59 percent were unimplemented.
